title: Capacity oscillation stabilizer and predictive tenant throttling
creator: Priya Nair
description: Post-incident follow-up addressing a recent dedicated-cluster capacity oscillation where recurrent short spikes from several tenants caused cascading eviction events and long tail latencies. This ticket implements a stabilizer composed of predictive tenant throttling, burst-credit smoothing, and eviction hysteresis so we avoid rapid reservation resizing and noisy-tenant churn. The goal is to reduce tail latency and evictions while preserving legitimate burst capacity for latency-sensitive workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction rate in canary clusters reduced by >= 60% for same load profile compared to baseline
95th percentile tail latency for affected routes improved by >= 30% under bursty tenant mix
Automatic reservation adjustments are limited to <= 1 change per tenant per 10m during noisy periods
New dashboard surfaces per-tenant burst-credit, smoothed-utilization, and predictive-throttle score
Runbook updated with step-by-step mitigation and rollback for predictive throttling changes
tasks: Instrument new telemetry: per-tenant short-window moving-average GPU utilization, token-bucket credits, recent eviction_count; emit to telemetry-prod (ENG-88342-T1)
Prototype predictive-throttle model: exponential smoothing + peak detection to produce a 0-100 throttle score (ENG-88342-T2)
Implement burst-credit smoothing: change token-bucket refill to weighted refill with hysteresis switch (ENG-88342-T3)
Eviction hysteresis: delay eviction-trigger by configurable grace window and add backoff between reservation downsizes (ENG-88342-T4)
Add autoscaler gating: autoscaler cannot reduce reservation size while predictive-throttle > threshold unless manual override (ENG-88342-T5)
Create canary pipeline: deploy on two small dedicated clusters, run synthetic workload harness, and compare metrics (ENG-88342-T6)
Dashboard & alerts: new Grafana panels + alert rules for predictive-throttle > 70 and frequent reservation changes (ENG-88342-T7)
Docs & runbook: document behavior, knobs, and rollback steps (ENG-88342-T8)
Post-deploy smoke: 6h observation window before wide rollout; gather customer-impacting traces (ENG-88342-T9)

postmortem_summary: Root cause: rapid reactive reservation resizing combined with un-smoothed burst tokens allowed short noisy tenants to exhaust shared capacity, triggering allocator evictions that then caused autoscaler to oscillate. Contributing factors: limited short-window telemetry, lack of eviction hysteresis, and no predictive throttle to separate legitimate bursts from pathological noise.

Update Dedicated runbook and customer-facing incident template
